patterns.label: querer + infinitive
patterns.rule: Conjugate querer for the person, then leave the activity verb in the infinitive. Querer changes e → ie except in nosotros: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, quieren.
patterns.meaning: I want to cook dinner.

patterns.label: necesitar + infinitive
patterns.rule: Conjugate necesitar for the person; the second verb stays in the infinitive. Put no before necesitar to make the sentence negative.
patterns.meaning: We need to buy rice.

patterns.label: ir a + infinitive
patterns.rule: Use present-tense ir + a + an infinitive to express a plan: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. The a is essential. This is a future meaning expressed with present ir, rather than a simple-future ending.
patterns.meaning: We are going to cook dinner.

patterns.label: tener que + infinitive
patterns.rule: Conjugate tener, keep que, and leave the activity in the infinitive: tengo que trabajar, tenemos que salir.
patterns.meaning: I have to study today.

patterns.label: levantarse: me / te / se / nos / se
patterns.rule: Use the reflexive pronoun that matches the subject before the conjugated verb: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, se levantan.
patterns.meaning: I get up at seven.

patterns.label: me gusta / me gustan
patterns.rule: In this pattern the thing liked controls the verb: me gusta el café, me gustan los tacos. An infinitive takes singular gusta: me gusta cocinar.
patterns.meaning: I like cooking.

patterns.label: poder + infinitive
patterns.rule: Conjugate poder and keep the next verb in the infinitive: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.
patterns.meaning: Can I pay by card?

patterns.label: lo / la before a conjugated verb
patterns.rule: Lo replaces a masculine singular direct object; la replaces a feminine singular one. In these simple sentences place it before the conjugated verb.
patterns.meaning: I buy it today. It refers to el pan.

patterns.label: hay / estar
patterns.rule: Use hay to introduce the existence of something. Use estar to locate an identified person or thing: hay una farmacia; la farmacia está cerca.
patterns.example: Hay un banco cerca de aquí.
patterns.meaning: There is a bank near here.

patterns.label: preterite + ayer
patterns.rule: Use the preterite for these completed events. Regular -ar yo uses -é; nosotros uses -amos. The written accent distinguishes cociné from cocine.
patterns.meaning: Yesterday I cooked rice.

patterns.label: fui / hice
patterns.rule: Ir has preterite forms fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron. Hacer uses hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicieron. Context distinguishes fui as went or was.
patterns.meaning: Yesterday I went to the market.

patterns.label: imperfect + antes
patterns.rule: In these sentences the imperfect presents a habitual past situation: trabajaba, comía, vivía. Regular -ar uses -aba; -er and -ir use -ía.
patterns.meaning: I used to work at home.

patterns.label: imperfect background + preterite event
patterns.rule: The imperfect supplies the ongoing background; the preterite presents the bounded event: cocinaba cuando sonó el teléfono. The choice follows how the speaker presents the situation.
patterns.meaning: I was cooking when the phone rang.

patterns.label: había + past participle
patterns.rule: The past perfect uses imperfect haber + a participle. The participle stays unchanged: había comido, habíamos comido. Use it here for an event already complete before another past event.
patterns.example: Cuando llegué, Ana ya había salido.
patterns.meaning: When I arrived, Ana had already left.

patterns.label: haber + past participle
patterns.rule: The present perfect uses present haber + a participle: he visitado, hemos visto. These tasks target experience up to now. Mexico often uses the preterite in contexts where Spain uses the perfect; both choices depend on context and region.
patterns.meaning: I have never visited Puebla. Use the present perfect.

patterns.label: simple future
patterns.rule: Add the future ending to the infinitive: llamaré, llamaremos. Some verbs have irregular stems, such as haré and tendré.
patterns.meaning: I will call you tomorrow.

patterns.label: podría / debería / me gustaría
patterns.rule: The conditional can soften requests and advice: ¿podrías ayudarme?, deberías descansar. Poder has the irregular stem podr-; gustar and deber use the infinitive plus conditional endings.
patterns.meaning: Could you help me? Use tú and the conditional.

patterns.label: si + present, future
patterns.rule: For these realistic future conditions, use present indicative after si and future in the result: si tengo tiempo, iré. Do not use the simple future directly after this conditional si.
patterns.meaning: If I have time, I will call you.

patterns.label: querer que + subjunctive
patterns.rule: Use quiero + infinitive for your own action, but quiero que + a conjugated subjunctive for a different person: quiero que vengas. Venir has venga, vengas, venga, vengamos, vengan.
patterns.meaning: I want you to come early. Use tú.

patterns.label: es importante que + subjunctive
patterns.rule: In these evaluations, es importante que and es mejor que take the subjunctive. Keep que before the clause: es importante que descanses.
patterns.meaning: It is important that you rest. Use tú.

patterns.label: cuando + future-reference subjunctive
patterns.rule: Cuando takes present subjunctive when the event is still pending: te llamaré cuando llegue. For a habitual fact, it can take indicative. The main clause may be future.
patterns.example: Te llamaré cuando llegue a casa.
patterns.meaning: I will call you when I get home.

patterns.label: creo que / no creo que
patterns.rule: An affirmative creo que normally asserts an opinion with indicative. These negative no creo que clauses use subjunctive: creo que tiene razón; no creo que tenga razón.
patterns.example: No creo que Ana tenga razón.
patterns.meaning: I do not think Ana is right.

patterns.label: busco algo que + subjunctive
patterns.rule: A relative clause about a desired but unidentified thing can use subjunctive: busco un hotel que tenga piscina. Indicative presents an identified or asserted example: conozco un hotel que tiene piscina.
patterns.example: Busco un hotel que tenga piscina.
patterns.meaning: I am looking for a hotel that has a pool. No specific hotel is identified.

patterns.label: para + infinitive / para que + subjunctive
patterns.rule: Use para + infinitive when the subject of purpose stays the same. Use para que + subjunctive when another subject performs the intended action: te llamo para que sepas.
patterns.example: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
patterns.meaning: I am explaining it to you so that you understand it.

patterns.label: si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional
patterns.rule: Use imperfect subjunctive in the hypothetical si clause and conditional in its result: si tuviera tiempo, viajaría. The -se subjunctive series is also accepted.
patterns.meaning: If I had time, I would travel more.

patterns.label: me pidió que + imperfect subjunctive
patterns.rule: After the past request me pidió que, use imperfect subjunctive for the requested action: me pidió que viniera. This reports a request, not an assertion that it happened.
patterns.example: Ana me pidió que viniera temprano.
patterns.meaning: Ana asked me to come early.

patterns.label: si + hubiera, habría + participle
patterns.rule: Use si + hubiera/hubiese + participle for an unreal past condition. These tasks use habría + participle for the result. The participles do not agree with the subject.
patterns.meaning: If I had studied, I would have passed.

patterns.label: se vende / se venden / se vive
patterns.rule: In passive se constructions the verb agrees with the thing: se venden boletos. Impersonal se has no subject and uses singular: se vive bien aquí. These are different uses of se.
patterns.meaning: Tickets are sold here. Use se.

patterns.label: dijo que + imperfect / conditional
patterns.rule: With a past reporting verb, a present situation may be reported with imperfect: dijo que estaba cansada. A future promise can become conditional: dijo que vendría. The exact shift depends on the reporting context.
patterns.meaning: Ana said that she was tired.

patterns.label: aunque + indicative / subjunctive
patterns.rule: Aunque with indicative here asserts a known fact. With subjunctive here it presents a hypothetical or conceded possibility: aunque llueva, saldremos. These are contextual choices, not a rule based on the word aunque alone.
patterns.meaning: Even if it rains tomorrow, we will go out. Treat rain as a possibility.

patterns.label: sin embargo / por lo tanto
patterns.rule: Sin embargo marks contrast; por lo tanto introduces a consequence. Choose the connector from the relation between the ideas, not merely from the punctuation.
patterns.example: El plan es caro; sin embargo, puede funcionar.
patterns.meaning: The plan is expensive; however, it can work. Use sin embargo.

patterns.label: parecería que / no necesariamente
patterns.rule: Conditional parecería can soften an interpretation. No necesariamente limits a generalisation. Neither expression turns a possibility into an established fact.
patterns.example: Parecería que el problema es más complejo.
patterns.meaning: It would seem that the problem is more complex. Use parecería que.

patterns.label: si bien / aun así
patterns.rule: Si bien introduces a concession presented here as a fact. Aun así means even so and does not carry a written accent on aun in this expression.
patterns.example: Si bien la medida es útil, no resuelve todo.
patterns.meaning: While the measure is useful, it does not solve everything. Use si bien.

patterns.label: es decir / mejor dicho / no se trata de
patterns.rule: Es decir restates or clarifies an idea. Mejor dicho corrects or refines an earlier wording. No se trata de X, sino de Y redirects the focus; the contrast needs sino after the negation.
patterns.example: Es una medida temporal; es decir, no será permanente.
patterns.meaning: It is a temporary measure; that is, it will not be permanent. Use es decir.

patterns.label: según / mientras que
patterns.rule: Según introduces an attributed viewpoint. Mientras que can contrast two positions. In mediation, preserve who believes what and keep any uncertainty in the source.
patterns.example: Según Ana, el plan es viable.
patterns.meaning: According to Ana, the plan is viable. Use según.

patterns.label: habrá + participle
patterns.rule: Future perfect can mark completion before a future deadline: para mañana habremos terminado. It can also express a conjecture about a completed event: no contesta; habrá salido. The second use is an inference, not certainty.
patterns.example: Para mañana habremos terminado el informe.
patterns.meaning: By tomorrow we will have finished the report.

patterns.label: habit / background versus completed event
patterns.rule: Choose the imperfect for a habit, ongoing background or description in these contexts. Choose the preterite for the event presented as bounded or complete. A time expression alone does not determine the tense: compare antes caminaba with ayer caminé.
patterns.meaning: I was cooking when the phone rang.
